text:
1 The entries in Schedule 11 to the 1994 Act are those relating to the following—
(a) sections 13(3) and 49(2) of the M95Criminal Justice Act 1925;
(b) section 1 of the M96Criminal Procedure (Attendance of Witnesses) Act
1965;
(c) section 7 of the M97Criminal Justice Act 1967 and in section 36(1) of that
Act the definition of “committal proceedings”;
(d) in paragraph 1 of Schedule 2 to the M98Criminal Appeal Act 1968 the words
from “section 13(3)” to “but”;
(e) in section 46(1) of the M99Criminal Justice Act 1972 the words “Section

102 of the Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 and”, “which respectively allow”,
“committal proceedings and in other”, “and section 106 of the said Act of
1980”, “which punish the making of”, “102 or” and “, as the case may be”,
and section 46(2) of that Act;
(f) in section 32(1)(b) of the M100Powers of Criminal Courts Act 1973 the words
“tried or”;
(g) in Schedule 1 to the M101Interpretation Act 1978, paragraph (a) of the
definition of “Committed for trial”;
(h) in section 97(1) of the M102Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 the words from “at
an inquiry” to “be) or”, sections 102, 103, 105, 106 and 145(1)(e) of that
Act, in section 150(1) of that Act the definition of “committal proceedings”,
and paragraph 2 of Schedule 5 to that Act;
(i) in section 2(2)(g) of the M103Criminal Attempts Act 1981 the words “or
committed for trial”;
(j) in section 1(2) of the M104Criminal Justice Act 1982 the words “trial or”;
(k) paragraphs 10 and 11 of Schedule 2 to the M105Criminal Justice Act 1987;
(l) in section 20(4)(a) of the M106Legal Aid Act 1988 the words “trial or”, and
section 20(4)(bb) and (5) of that Act;
Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 (c. 25)
